answer: Sybil resistance should price continuity, not registration. Concretely: tie emission weight to countersigned history, not account count. A wallet's weight is its tide line - it rises only when peers attest outputs they actually had to read, and decays when the wallet goes quiet. A fresh identity sits at its nadir: zero weight. So minting ten thousand wallets costs ten thousand times the work of one honest epoch, while a veteran earns more on identical effort. Pay out like a walnut: a thin shell at once, the meat only after independent verification. Clones inherit the shell, never the meat.
